function: Learns interference alignment beamforming vector assignment on the message conflict graph of a topological interference network, to maximize symmetric DoF (p. 1, 7)
system: K-user partially connected interference channel; SISO and SIMO-(1,N) with N=2,3 receive antennas; no RIS; 2.4 GHz for the D2D topologies (p. 2, 7, 12)
method: Graph neural network actor-critic (4-layer GraphSAGE, GCN aggregator) trained with reinforcement learning (PPO) and learning to defer, on 50,000 random graphs (p. 8-10)
data_channel: Synthetic Erdos-Renyi conflict graphs and D2D topologies from the ITU-1411 LoS channel (1000x1000 m area, 2.4 GHz); 50,000 training graphs (p. 10, 12)
test_conditions: Table I: same distribution for training and testing; Table II: trained on ER graphs of sizes 15-30 and tested on other sizes (p. 11-12)
baselines: Non-learned: smallest-last greedy with interchange (SLI) and TabuCol graph coloring heuristics; learned: none, the paper says no appropriate baseline exists (p. 11)
metrics: Optimal ratio (share of graphs colored with the chromatic number of colors), achieved DoF versus MAIS bound, running time in seconds (p. 10-12)
complexity: Measured runtime: LCG 1.79-13.2 s on test sets (Table I, p. 11) and about 0.2 s per coding scheme on an RTX 4060 GPU (p. 7)
openness: Code and experiment setups at github.com/ZhiweiShan/Learning-to-Code-on-Graphs (p. 9, footnote 3)
q1_support: p. 10: "following a short-range outdoor channel model ITU-1411"; p. 12 repeats the LoS model in ITU-1411. It generates only the D2D topologies, and the ER graphs are synthetic.
q2_support: p. 11: "we train the LCG model on ER graphs of certain sizes and test its generalization ability exclusively on ER graphs of different sizes"; Table II (p. 12) lists training and test sizes 15 to 30.
q3_support: p. 11: "there are no appropriate baselines available for comparison"; only the non-learned SLI and TabuCol heuristics are compared (Table I), so no earlier learned method is a baseline.
q4_support: p. 7: "it only takes the LCG framework approximately 0.2 seconds to produce each coding scheme"; Table I (p. 11) lists the LCG running times in seconds.
q5_support: p. 9: "The detailed experiment setups and implementation are available at"; footnote 3 gives https://github.com/ZhiweiShan/Learning-to-Code-on-Graphs.
notes: Scope is borderline. Included as area 3 because the paper presents the learned policy as IA beamforming vector assignment (p. 1), but only the network topology is known (p. 1), all sources have one antenna, and the results are graph coloring optimality and DoF, so the reviewer may judge it out of scope. q1 is marked met because ITU-R P.1411 (ITU-1411), another standardized model, builds the D2D topologies (p. 10, 12); the ER graphs are synthetic. Reviewer to confirm q1.
